page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text; running head at top; page number top left; faint show-through from the reverse side throughout (not transcribed); no marginal notes of substance.

main_text.p: bertatem ferre possit, sub leni imperio lasciviens, sub aspero fatiscens, sub utroque contra imperantem insurgens, siqué conatus ejus metu superioris potentiæ compescatur, querelis se ulciscens, adeò, ut omnibus animalibus facilius sit imperare, quàm homini, citiusque inveniatur vir fortis, qui hostem superet, quàm qui civem, annon ita? Ecquales hinc porrò res utrisque substratæ, annon singulares, ideoque infinitæ, saltem indefinitæ, variisque circumstantiis quasi fasciis involutæ, atque ita quidem involutæ, ut humanis consiliis sæpenumerò explicari nequeant, nisi Deus Ἀντὶ μηχανῆς, cujus auspicis auxilium implorandum, ut olim rustici invocârunt numen Cereris, antequam terræ mandarent semina, nisi, inquam, Deus nobis præsentem opem ferat, suâque scientia nostram insciitiam, potentiâ impotentiam sarciat, atquè non raró res sint sic satis expeditæ, nec deest etiam magistratui animus expediendi, sed nec subditis adsit animus impediendi, tamen eventus earum multoties reguntur occultis causis, ita ut optimè consulta pessimè cadant, præclarissimique conatus in spongiam incumbant, atque in nervum erumpant vel tandem, Jovis interim taxillis semper cadentibus benè in hâc vitæ humanæ Tragico-Comœdiâ, & Comico-Tragœdiâ. Cæterùm, quæ tumultuariè confignavi de difficultate hujus studii, ea non in siniftram accipi velim partem, Auditores, quasi animo absterrendi hæc ziza-nia seram, verùm in dexteram, ut ipsa difficultas stimulum

page.notes: Greek phrase in the line "nisi Deus" is printed as ἀντὶ μηχανῆς (partly obscured by the scan). Show-through from the reverse page is visible and was not transcribed. Last line "mulum" is set right-aligned at the foot and is a catchword-like continuation of "stimulum"; left as printed.
